did.unittitle: Jack Briggs collection
did.abstract: Photographic prints (31), and assorted personal documents, chiefly related to the tenure of Jack Briggs (1920-2006) as Commandant of Police in Dubai (1965-1975). Includes photographs of Briggs with the ruler of Dubai, Sheikh Rashid bin Sa'id al-Maktoum, and other regional rulers, including Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan al-Nahyan of Abu Dhabi (later ruler of the United Arab Emirates). The documents are chiefly diplomas for coursework completed at British universities, but also include a handwritten decree from King Hussein of Jordan.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions governing access
accessrestrict.p: The Jack Briggs Collection is open and available for use in the Archives and Special Collections department of the New York University Abu Dhabi Library.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The Jack Briggs collection is arranged into two series: Documents and Photographs, with the former arranged in largely chronological order, and the latter in rough alphabetic order by name of those depicted in the images.

bioghist.head: Biographical note
bioghist.p: Jack Briggs, OBE (1920-2006) was born in London on 28 May 1920, to Herman and Annie (nee Thatcher) Briggs. Although born in London, Briggs spent most of his childhood in Lancashire, attending school in Accrington, before leaving school at age 14. When World War II broke out, he enlisted with the British Army, with the Scots Guards, in 1940. Soon thereafter he answered a notice requesting volunteers, and was sent to Mandate Palestine to be trained as a police officer. He served in Palestine for seven years, learning and developing what proved to be a lasting interest in the Arabic language, but then returned to Britain where he worked as a police officer.

A short time later, however, Briggs returned to the Middle East, taking up a position as a police officer in Bahrain, before transferring to Qatar, where he was appointed as Commandant of Police in Doha. While in Doha, he met and married Mary Catherine Laverty in April 1953, with whom he subsequently had four children. In 1964, after the Trucial Oman Scouts formed a police wing, Briggs moved to Sharjah when he was appointed as commander of that force, with the rank of major. He was soon seconded to the police force in the neighboring emirate of Dubai, where he was appointed Commandant of Police in 1965. By this time, he had become fluent in Arabic, and developed a close friendship with the ruler of Dubai, Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed al-Maktoum (1912-1990), and played a fundamental role in the development of the police force there during the decade he served in that position. When he stepped down from that position in 1975, he remained in Dubai, serving as an advisor to the police force and to Sheikh Rashid, until his retirement in 1986.

His fluency in Arabic led him to continue to study that language, earning degrees from the University of London, and leading him to work as a translator. Among the works he translated was the collection of short stories by Mohammed al-Murr, "The Wink of the Mona Lisa, and other stories from the Gulf" (Dubai: Motivate Publishing, 1994). He moved permanently back to England in 1996, settling in Hampshire, but traveled to Dubai frequently. An avid cyclist, he died of a heart attack while participating in a race in Hampshire in July 2006.
Sources: Obituary, by James Craig. The Guardian, 7 August 2006. Obituary, by Alia al-Theeb. Gulf News, 31 July 2006. Public records (birth, baptism, death, marriage), Ancestry.com

scopecontent.head: Content Description
scopecontent.p: Photographic prints (31), and assorted personal documents, chiefly related to the tenure of Jack Briggs (1920-2006) as Commandant of Police in Dubai (1965-1975). Includes photographs of Briggs with the ruler of Dubai, Sheikh Rashid bin Sa'id al-Maktoum, and other regional rulers, including Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan al-Nahyan of Abu Dhabi (later ruler of the United Arab Emirates). The documents are chiefly diplomas for coursework completed at British universities, but also include a handwritten decree from King Hussein of Jordan.

Most of the photographs appear to be copy prints of works by Noor Ali Rashid, who worked as an official photographer for the ruling family of Dubai, and often portray the ruler, Sheikh Rashid bin Saaed al Maktoum, and members of his family, with various guests. Many of the images appear to have been taken at the airport in Dubai, usually with Briggs present, and either with ceremonial reception stages in the background, aircraft hangars, aircraft, and automobiles. Other rulers in these images include Sheikh Isa bin Salman al-Khalifa, the ruler of Bahrain; Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan al-Nahyan, ruler of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and later leader of the United Arab Emirates; Hardan al-Tikriti, Air Marshal of the Iraqi Air Force; and Sheikh Rashid's sons, Hamdan and Maktoum, with images of the latter likely from the 1990s, following Sheikh Rashid's death and the accession of Sheikh Maktoum to the position of ruler of Dubai.
Very few of the photographs have any captions, dates, or other identifying information, and many of the individuals depicted are not yet identified.
